children: The S&P 500's recent rebound, improving momentum and historically tight volatility are creating a potentially favorable setup for the fourth quarter, according to Donovan Jackson, editor of The Chart Report.
The S&P 500 posted its best session in more than a month on Sept. 21 as the index rebounded from oversold conditions and moved to within 1% of a fresh all-time closing high.

Jackson noted that extremely tight Bollinger Bandwidth heading into October has preceded some of the market's biggest upside moves over the past decade. The current combination of compressed volatility, favorable seasonal trends and improving momentum could therefore provide a catalyst for a stronger finish to the year, according to The Chart Report.
Jackson also pointed to the four-year election cycle, which is approaching what has historically been a favorable period for equities.

Several areas of the market are showing signs of improving technical strength. Technology has broken above a downtrend line while also improving relative to the S&P 500, while semiconductors are breaking out from a multi-month consolidation.
The Magnificent Seven ETF has also moved to new all-time highs, highlighting renewed strength among some of the market's largest technology stocks.
The semiconductor setup could be particularly important for technology investors. In a separate Sept. 21 note, Jackson said the Semiconductor ETF
was moving above its all-time-high anchored VWAP after spending several months consolidating following its record three-month rally.
A sustained breakout could signal that semiconductors are resuming their longer-term uptrend, although a failed breakout could indicate that the group needs more time to consolidate.

title: S&P 500 rebound, tight volatility set stage for potential Q4 upside
